title: publish install and upgrade print fleet upgrade --dry-run, which fleet upgrade refuses
body:
Found by dc on 2026-09-16, running the 0069 fleet sweep on hv's go. Reproduced.

After a publish-upgrade, `bin/devbin upgrade` in devbin's own tree ends with:

    The estate still carries the OLD bytes until each project upgrades:
      bin/devbin fleet upgrade --dry-run

Running that line exactly as printed refuses:

    devbin: unknown argument '--dry-run' (try: devbin fleet upgrade --help)

`fleet upgrade` has no `--dry-run`: a dry run is its default, and `--apply` is the only flag (`bin/.devbin/cmd/fleet`, `fleet upgrade --help`). The same wrong line is printed by the publish branch of `install` (`lib/cmd/install:371`) as well as by `lib/cmd/upgrade:123`.

## Why it is worth an issue

It is the next-step line printed at the moment an operator has just replaced the machine install and the whole estate is behind it. The refusal is harmless -- the parser is strict, so nothing runs -- but a remedy line that does not run teaches the reader to stop trusting the remedy lines.

## Shape of a fix, not a ruling

Print `bin/devbin fleet upgrade` (it previews and writes nothing), in both places, from one home. Hold it with an arm that runs the printed line and asserts it is accepted -- a test of the string alone would pass the moment both sites were edited to agree on a wrong one.
